title: Lava, Ash and Pyroclastic Flows
objective: After this level you can name what an eruption releases and explain why pyroclastic flows are the deadliest.
summary: Eruptions release slow lava, hard glassy ash and gas (mostly water vapor). The deadliest product is the pyroclastic flow, a fast, scorching avalanche of rock and gas.

cards.headline: The lava is usually the least of your worries.
cards.body: Most lava flows move slowly enough to get out of the way. An eruption releases much more: ash, gas and, most dangerous of all, pyroclastic flows. Here's what comes out, and why the fastest one is the deadliest.

cards.headline: Lava: slow but unstoppable
cards.body: Because most lava flows move slowly, they rarely kill anyone directly. But everything that can't move is knocked over, buried or set on fire. Lava can bury homes and farmland under tens of meters of rock. You can walk away from lava; your house can't.

cards.headline: Ash and gas
cards.body: Volcanic ash isn't soft like ash from a campfire. It's jagged bits of rock, minerals and volcanic glass smaller than 2 mm: hard, abrasive, and carried by wind for thousands of miles. The gas is mostly harmless water vapor, plus carbon dioxide and sulfur dioxide. Remember Level 1? That sulfur dioxide can form droplets high in the sky that reflect sunlight and cool the planet.

cards.headline: Pyroclastic flows: the deadliest
cards.body: A pyroclastic flow is a hot mix of lava blocks, pumice, ash and gas that races across the ground, typically faster than 80 km per hour, at 200 to 700 °C. It knocks down, buries or carries away nearly everything in its path. That's why it's considered the deadliest volcano hazard. In 1902, one from Mount Pelée destroyed the town of Saint-Pierre on Martinique.

cards.headline: Eruptions: unpacked
learned: Ash is hard, jagged rock and glass

questions.prompt: What is volcanic ash actually made of?

options.label: Soft soot from burning trees
options.rationale: Volcanic ash isn't made by burning.

options.label: Frozen droplets of volcanic gas
options.rationale: Ash is solid rock and glass.

options.label: Jagged bits of rock, minerals and volcanic glass
Salt left over from boiled seawater
options.rationale: Ash comes from shattered rock and glass.

questions.explanation: Volcanic ash is hard, abrasive fragments of rock, minerals and glass smaller than 2 mm.

questions.prompt: Match each thing a volcano releases with its description.
questions.explanation: Lava is slow but unstoppable, volcanic ash is jagged bits of rock, the gas is mostly harmless water vapor, and a pyroclastic flow is the deadliest volcano hazard.

questions.prompt: The volcanic gas that links back to Level 1's story of an eruption cooling the planet is _____.

options.label: water vapor
options.rationale: It's the most abundant gas, but not the cooling one.

options.label: carbon dioxide
options.rationale: It isn't the gas that reflects sunlight.

options.label: nitrogen
options.rationale: Nitrogen isn't the cooling gas here.

questions.explanation: Sulfur dioxide turns into sulfuric acid droplets high in the atmosphere that reflect sunlight and cool the surface.
